sections.title: About the Role
blocks: House of Marketers is entering its **next stage of growth**. As the business becomes larger, the challenge is not simply doing more. It is making sure **revenue can grow without cost, headcount, complexity and CEO involvement growing at the same rate.**

The Head of Operations owns the **operating infrastructure** behind the business: the systems, controls, data, accountability structures and operational functions that allow teams to perform at a high level and leadership to **see problems before they become firefighting.**
This is **not an administrative role, and it is not a Delivery role.**

Functional leaders remain accountable for the performance of their areas. The Head of Operations creates the **additional layer of visibility, control and accountability** that makes sure those outcomes are actually being achieved.
The role reports directly to the CEO.

items.title: Commercial Operations and Control
blocks: The Head of Operations builds the **controls that help the business deliver against its commercial targets** and identify problems early.

Delivery remains accountable for campaign performance and margin. The Delivery Director will own this across the function, with Senior Campaign Managers accountable for their campaigns until that role is in place.
Operations owns the **infrastructure around that accountability.**
This includes

list: visibility into creator costs, campaign delays, resourcing and other drivers affecting performance
escalation when results move away from plan
identifying recurring causes rather than repeatedly fixing individual cases

blocks: The goal is to give the CEO an **additional layer of control without taking ownership away from Delivery.**

items.title: Forecasting, Capacity and Resource Planning
blocks: The Head of Operations owns the **operational models** used to understand **what the business is likely to need next.**
The role combines live pipeline, campaign data, workload, timelines, historical delivery patterns and team capacity to predict

list: what different pipeline scenarios mean for the team

blocks: This should allow the business to **make resource decisions before teams become overloaded** or delivery is affected.

items.title: Systems, Automation and Data
blocks: The Head of Operations owns the **roadmap for operational systems, automation and AI.**
The role identifies where manual work, disconnected systems or poor data are **costing the business time or money**, then decides what should be fixed or built.
This includes areas such as margin controls, forecasting, target tracking, reporting, CRM and project management integrations, workflow automation and internal AI tools.
The Head of Operations manages the people responsible for building and maintaining this infrastructure.
Every significant project should have a **clear return** through time saved, cost reduced, additional capacity, better control or revenue enabled.

items.title: People and Organisational Performance
blocks: The Head of Operations owns the **structure around how people are managed and held accountable.**
This includes

list: coordination with specialist HR and legal support

blocks: The Head of Operations oversees the People Operations function and **remains accountable for its output.**
The role also reviews **how the organisation needs to change as the company grows**, including when new management layers, roles or functions are required.

items.title: Cross-Functional Operations and CEO Support
blocks: The Head of Operations owns operational issues and projects that **sit across several teams** or do not naturally belong to one functional leader.

This can include company-wide process changes, new systems, vendor changes, restructuring workflows, improving reporting or solving recurring problems between Sales, Delivery, Finance, People and Technology.
The role is to make sure there is **a clear owner, a decision is made and the work gets completed.**
The Head of Operations also makes sure **the CEO does not need to personally investigate every operational issue.**
When something genuinely needs CEO involvement, the Head of Operations should already understand **what happened, why it happened, who owns it, what has been done and what decision is required.**

sections.title: Functions Under Operations
blocks: The Head of Operations oversees and builds the **central operational functions** required as the company scales.
These may include:

list: selected functions temporarily sitting under Operations until the appropriate senior owner exists

blocks: This currently includes Social Media until ownership moves under the appropriate senior Marketing function.
The Head of Operations sets expectations for these functions, reviews performance and holds their owners accountable.
**Delegating execution does not remove the Head of Operations’ accountability** for the functions reporting into the role.

sections.title: What Success Looks Like
blocks: The role is succeeding when:

list: **The business scales more effectively** with stronger use of people, technology, data and resources as the company grows.
**Performance is controlled earlier** with margin, capacity and operational risks visible before they become problems and clear owners accountable for action.
**Better data drives better decisions** across forecasting, hiring, workload, resource allocation and operational planning.
**Technology creates measurable value** through time saved, lower cost, additional capacity, stronger control or better visibility.
**People perform with clearer accountability** through measurable targets, stronger management and faster time to productivity.
**The CEO gets time back** because issues are resolved at the right level and leadership receives clear recommendations instead of raw problems.

blocks: **The company becomes more controlled, more efficient and easier to operate as it grows.**
